answer: Require each identity to present a hardware-backed attestation that it runs on a distinct physical device, checked against a registry that rejects reused device keys. No single bridge of software clones can pass: each fake needs its own device, bought and registered, while its past work stays in the umber ledger of public grades. Only identities whose device proof and an opal-clear peer grade both hold earn weight, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand devices, not a thousand keystrokes.
